content: We rejected Mastra because suspend/resume durability violated the Factory invariants.

Every step in a Factory run must be replayable from the event log alone. No step may read mutable state that is not captured in its input envelope, because a replay that consults live state is not a replay, it is a second execution wearing a costume.

When the scheduler starved long-running jobs in March, we fixed it by weighting the queue by age rather than by priority alone. The same shape of starvation later appeared in the retry queue and the identical fix applied there.
Lee prefers that agent prompts live in versioned files under prompts/ rather than inline string literals, so that a prompt change shows up as a reviewable diff instead of hiding inside a code edit.
Runs are identified by ULID rather than UUIDv4, so log lines sort chronologically without needing a separate timestamp index.

The first draft of the retry policy was sent back. Exponential backoff without jitter produced synchronized thundering herds against the model provider, and the reviewer would not accept it until randomized spread was added.
Factory must run with no outbound network access in the sealed evaluation environment. Anything that requires a live API call has to be stubbed at the port boundary before it can be exercised there.
We cap concurrent worker processes at eight. Beyond that the shared SQLite journal became the bottleneck and throughput went flat, so more workers bought nothing but contention.
We have twice tried to make the orchestrator language-agnostic through a plugin ABI, and both times abandoned it after the serialization overhead exceeded the cost of the work being delegated.
Error messages in Factory should name the file and the fix, not merely the failed assertion. A message the operator cannot act on is a bug report filed against us, not against them.
Human approval checkpoints are stored as first-class events rather than as blocking prompts, so a paused run can be picked up later by a different operator on a different machine.
No agent may write outside its assigned worktree. The supervisor rejects any patch that touches paths above the sprint boundary, no matter how small or how obviously correct the change looks.
The dashboard rewrite was accepted with one reservation: it polls every 500ms and will have to move to server-sent events before we onboard more than a dozen simultaneous runs.
Model choice per step is declared up front in the sprint plan rather than inferred at runtime, so the cost of a run is predictable before it starts rather than discovered in the invoice.
Atlas ingests everything as append-only raw partitions first and only then derives typed tables, so a bad parser can be rerun without re-fetching anything from upstream.
Personally identifying columns must be tokenized before they leave the landing zone. Downstream jobs never see raw email addresses or phone numbers, and no exception has been granted for debugging.

We once let a vendor CSV drive the schema and then spent a quarter unwinding it when their column order changed silently. Since then every external feed passes through an explicit mapping file that we own.
Backfills run in a separate resource pool from scheduled jobs, so a six-month replay cannot delay the morning refresh.
The team prefers declarative transforms over imperative scripts, largely because the dependency graph is then derivable from the code rather than described in a document that drifts.

The deduplication pass was rejected on the grounds that it used wall-clock arrival order as the tiebreaker, which is not stable across retries. It was reworked to use the source sequence number instead.
No job may hold a warehouse connection for longer than fifteen minutes. Long operations must checkpoint and reconnect rather than sitting on a slot.
We store timestamps in UTC with an explicit source-timezone column rather than converting on write, after a daylight-saving transition silently shifted an entire day of records into the wrong bucket.

Every time we have computed freshness from job success alone it has lied to us. Freshness is now measured from the newest row actually present in the target table, never from the exit code of the loader.
Column names use snake_case and spell out the unit, so a duration field is called duration_ms and never just duration.
Late-arriving facts are handled with a merge on natural key rather than a delete-and-insert, so downstream incremental consumers never watch rows vanish and reappear between reads.
The nightly pipeline must finish before 06:00 local time or the finance close is blocked. Anything that pushes past that window needs explicit sign-off from the finance lead.
The first version of the lineage viewer was accepted, but the reviewer noted that it collapses multi-hop paths, which will mislead anyone tracing an incident more than two steps back.
We chose columnar Parquet over row-oriented Avro for the curated layer, because nearly every downstream read touches a handful of columns across a very large number of rows.
Every money amount is stored as an integer count of minor units together with an explicit currency code. Floating point never touches a balance.
Harbor is idempotent by client-supplied key on every mutating endpoint, because retries during a network partition are the normal case rather than an exceptional one.

The double-charge incident last spring traced back to a retry that generated a fresh idempotency key on each attempt. The rule since then is that the key is minted once by the caller and reused verbatim for the lifetime of the operation.
Refunds are recorded as new ledger entries rather than as reversals of the original, so the history of what actually happened stays intact and auditable.
Card data never enters our systems. The browser posts directly to the processor and we only ever hold a token, which keeps the compliance scope small enough for a team of our size.
The team would rather fail a payment loudly than succeed ambiguously. Any state we cannot reconcile is surfaced to an operator queue within the hour instead of being retried in silence.
The subscription proration logic was sent back twice. The first version billed a full partial month on downgrade, and the second lost a day at month boundaries in February.
We settled on a single reconciliation job that compares our ledger against the processor report every day, rather than treating webhooks as the system of record. Webhooks are a hint, not a truth.
Invoices, once issued, are immutable. A correction is a credit note plus a new invoice, which is what the auditors expect to see and what the tax authorities require.
We have been asked three separate times to support partial captures and each time the answer has been no, because our ledger model assumes a capture settles an authorization exactly once.

Dunning emails go out on a fixed schedule with a hard stop after four attempts. Past that point recovery rates were under one percent while complaints rose sharply, so the fifth message costs more than it earns.
Currency formatting is done at the edge in the user locale. The API always returns raw minor units plus the code and never a pre-formatted string.
The tax engine integration was accepted for launch but flagged as a single point of failure with no cached fallback, which will hurt us during their scheduled maintenance windows.
Lantern samples traces at ingest rather than at the client, so a service that suddenly becomes interesting can have its sampling raised without waiting for a redeploy.
Log lines must stay under 8 KB. The collector truncates anything longer mid-field, which corrupts the JSON and loses the whole event rather than just the tail.
The last two outages were both diagnosed from queue depth, not from CPU or memory. That is why the saturation dashboards now lead with depth and age instead of utilization.
Alerts should describe the symptom a user feels rather than the internal cause. An alert titled after a disk metric teaches nobody what actually broke.
Retention is thirty days hot and one year cold. The compliance ask was a year, but nobody has ever queried beyond a month interactively, so paying for fast storage past that was waste.
The alert-fatigue audit found that four rules produced sixty percent of all pages and that none of them had ever corresponded to a user-visible problem. All four were deleted rather than tuned.
Cardinality of any label set is capped at ten thousand series. Exceeding the cap drops that metric rather than degrading the whole store for everyone else.
We correlate logs to traces by injecting the trace id into the logging context at the middleware layer, rather than asking every call site to remember to pass it along.
Whenever we have added a dashboard without an owner it has rotted within two quarters. Every board now carries a named owner and a review date, and unowned boards are archived on sight.
Runbooks live next to the alert definition in the same file, because a runbook that requires a second search is a runbook nobody reads at 3am.
We rejected building our own storage layer and stayed on the managed offering, since our peak ingest is two orders of magnitude below the point where self-hosting starts to pay off.
Quill components ship as unstyled primitives plus a separate theme package, so a product team can adopt the behavior without inheriting our visual opinions.
Every interactive component must be fully operable with the keyboard alone and must announce state changes to screen readers. This is a launch blocker, not a polish item to be deferred.
We tried a CSS-in-JS runtime twice and reverted both times, because the hydration cost showed up plainly in our largest table view each time.
Design tokens are named by role rather than by value, so a token is called surface-raised and never gray-100.
The modal rework was rejected because it trapped focus correctly but never restored it to the trigger on close, which strands keyboard users in the page body with no obvious way back.

Breaking changes to a component ship behind a new major version of the package rather than behind a feature flag, since flags in a shared library never get cleaned up and quietly become permanent forks.
The bundle budget for the core package is 40 KB gzipped. A pull request that exceeds it fails CI rather than being waved through with a promise to fix it later.
Icons are inlined as SVG rather than loaded from a sprite sheet, because the sprite approach kept breaking under our content security policy.
Dark mode is implemented by swapping token values on a root attribute rather than by duplicating component styles, so a component author never writes a second set of rules.
The date picker was accepted with the note that its month grid rebuilds on every keystroke in the text field. That is fine at desktop scale and visibly janky on a low-end phone.
